entities.name: John M. Berrien
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
John Macpherson Berrien (1781–1856) was an American Democratic and later Whig politician from Georgia who served as U.S. Attorney General (1829–1831) under President Jackson and as U.S. Senator (1825–1829, 1841–1852) — serving three separate Senate terms across more than a quarter century. He resigned as Attorney General during the Petticoat Affair — the social crisis in Jackson's cabinet over the social status of Peggy Eaton, Secretary of War Eaton's wife — a seemingly trivial scandal that caused a genuine cabinet purge.

The Petticoat Affair was politically significant because it revealed Jackson's personal loyalty dynamics — his determination to defend Peggy Eaton caused his entire original cabinet to resign.

Berrien subsequently became a Whig and returned to the Senate where he served for over a decade.

He was a Georgia lawyer and senator for most of his adult life.
